decisions.statement: `auto` runs a pre-flight and takes kexec where the host is eligible, else dd.
Kernel lockdown, a disabled kexec load or enforcing Secure Boot leaves a host ineligible.
`dd` writes the metal raw image to the disk, makes a UEFI entry and reboots.
The kexec path leaves the disk write to the installer `akasha talos apply` triggers.
The run waits up to thirty minutes for maintenance mode to answer on the node.
ssh writes the remote script's own output to the streams the call was made on.
The node is named as a word or after `--node`.
Naming the node twice is refused.
A node the node table does not name is the caller's mistake.
A method that is not auto or kexec or dd is refused.
A node stating a disk selector rather than a disk takes the kexec method alone.
A run lacking `--confirm-wipe` is refused before the host is reached.
The schematic is registered before the host is reached.
The kexec script refuses rather than falling back to writing the disk.
The node answers at the address that node answered at before the handover.
The node is left in maintenance mode rather than in its cluster.
Every answer here is built by a function rather than written out as a value.
The handover is named as soon as the host has taken the script.
A run that threw after the handover names the handover in its refusal.
The reaching and the waiting this runs are handed in.
Nothing here undoes a disk wipe.

definition: the command replacing the Linux running on a remote node with Talos, over SSH
